My wife and I recently had the privilege of joining a small-group tour of Egypt with Egypt Guided Tours. If you’re looking for a well-organized experience that blends jam-packed days of fascinating history with time for relaxation and rejuvenation in 5-star surroundings, we can’t recommend this company highly enough!

Ahmed is a trained Egyptologist, and his depth of knowledge is exceptional. He has a real gift for teaching — explaining complex history in a way that is easy to follow, tying different sites and stories together, and repeating key points when necessary so that everything truly clicked. He made the entire experience both educational and engaging.

We were met at the airport, and never had to worry about anything from that point on. Even though we only had two full days in Cairo, the itinerary was incredibly rich. We explored the Stepped Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara, the pyramids of Khufu and Khafre in Giza, and even enjoyed a camel ride. We experienced a dinner cruise complete with belly dancers, a whirling dervish, and traditional Egyptian music. We also visited the Hanging Church and the Saints Sergius and Bacchus Church in Old Cairo, and spent time at the impressive new Grand Egyptian Museum. It was an amazing introduction to Cairo’s history and culture.

From Cairo we flew to Aswan, where we visited the stunning Philae Temple — a breathtaking site from the 3rd century BC. After a short night in Aswan, we travelled to Abu Simbel. The temples of Ramses II and his favourite wife Nefertari were truly awe-inspiring. From there, we boarded our Nile cruise for a luxurious three-night journey. Drifting along the river, exploring temples and a Nubian village along the way, and relaxing on deck as the scenery passed by made this part of the trip absolutely unforgettable.

When we arrived in Luxor, we visited the tombs in the Valley of the Kings, the temple of Queen Hatshepsut, and both the Karnac and Luxor temples. Somewhere in there we also managed to squeeze in a horse and carriage ride through the market and the streets of Luxor.

After a night in Luxor we had the incredible experience of a hot air balloon ride near the Valley of the Kings, floating over the breathtaking landscape at sunrise — an unforgettable way to take in Egypt’s history from above. Afterward, we drove to Hurghada where we spent three nights at a luxury all-inclusive resort. It was the perfect place to relax, unwind, and even snorkel in the Red Sea — a refreshing way to enjoy some fun in the sun after so many amazing adventures.

What made this trip truly exceptional was Ahmed’s professionalism and adaptability. When unforeseen circumstances required changes to the itinerary, he handled everything seamlessly, ensuring that nothing on our planned schedule was missed. He also guided us to wonderful local stops, including shops selling essential oils, carpets, alabaster, and spices, giving us a richer experience of Egyptian culture. Beyond his incredible knowledge and skill, we felt that we came as strangers and left as friends — his warmth, patience, and genuine care made him an unforgettable part of our journey.

We were unfortunately very disappointed with our stay at this guesthouse. The price was quite high, and we only discovered the next morning by accident that breakfast was not included — something that was not clearly indicated in the reservation information. In Egypt, it is very common for hotels and guesthouses to include breakfast, so this was an unpleasant surprise.

The room was also not properly prepared for two guests, as there was only one towel provided. We had to request another one on the first night. Hot water was another major issue: it was not available on our first night (we were too tired to report it), it worked briefly the next morning, and then we had no hot water again for the rest of our stay, which was extremely uncomfortable.

We also experienced a serious mosquito problem. Due to the location and the open balcony on the ground floor, mosquitoes constantly entered the room. They were very aggressive — I was bitten multiple times, and the bites remained red and itchy for nearly a week.

Additionally, the absence of security was concerning. The large ground-floor balcony opens directly onto the street, meaning anyone could easily walk in. There was also no one consistently present at reception to handle requests or monitor the premises.

Also discovered that Wi-Fi was charged extra first time I see this in my entire life !! Again this was not clearly indicated in the information during the reservation.

Although the owner tried to appear friendly, it did not feel genuine. When he became aware of our dissatisfaction regarding the hot water and breakfast, he avoided us at the time of departure instead of addressing the issues.

Overall, the stay did not meet our expectations. I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone especially that there are various much better options in Aswan for much more reasonable prices.

The Aswan Public Library is a major cultural landmark, representing a significant addition to the cultural landscape of Aswan. The symbolic significance of establishing the library near the tomb of the late Aswan writer Abbas Mahmoud Al-Aqqad is not arbitrary; a city that produced such a distinguished writer as Al-Aqqad deserves to have its people able to read, and this distinguished cultural center is a testament to that.

The library operates efficiently, offering a wide variety of activities, both those provided by the Cultural Activities Department and those offered by the Training Department. These activities cater to different age groups and fulfill the needs of both young and old for knowledge, learning, and acquiring new experiences.

The various workshops for children are excellent and diverse (beadwork, recycling, drawing, etc.). The library also hosts school students from across the governorate to introduce them to its services.

The library's reading rooms are also diverse and multi-purpose, including separate reading rooms for adults and children, as well as various activity rooms, a seminar room, a garden theater, and a reception hall.

The library occupies an area of ​​3200 square meters and comprises three floors, boasting a distinctive architectural design. In addition to the main auditorium and seminar rooms, the library includes a computer lab and an information and communications technology center.

I encourage everyone to visit the library and become a member to benefit from its excellent services.

The Cultural Activities Department, led by Professor Mustafa Muhammad Awad, is doing outstanding work.

I went on a five day four night trip with the folks at Western Desert Tour. My family and I were picked up in Luxor and we headed north to Dakhla Oasis before spending a few days out in the Agabat Valley, White Desert, and Black Desert. The two days we spent in the White Desert with our very knowledgeable and experienced guide and drivers were the absolute highlight of our entire trip in Egypt. Contrary to popular belief, the Western Desert is very safe and perfect for travellers.

The pace was just right and relaxing. Our guide, Mahmoud (?), and drivers (Rahman and I forget the other driver’s name), were very knowledgeable, fun to talk to and hang out with. They were always able to pick out the perfect campsite with great sunrise and sunset views. There were always options for each of us on the trip. I am an avid hiker and photographer; they gave me suggestions on where to hike around our campsite while my folks were able to chill out and just relax in the desert. The meals provided were varied and freshly prepared on the spot. The guys also involved my sister in the meal prep when they noticed that she took more of an interest in that than the desert really. Sleeping out under the stars by the fire is also an option for those so inclined. I highly recommend it. The stargazing in the desert is unparalleled. If you like sand boarding, that is possible as well. Adrenaline junkies can also get their fix from
the 4x4s traversing the lines of sand dunes and rough terrain. That being said, if you are set on hiking all day and already know the formations you want to visit, it is probably best to communicate that with Khalid, the owner, up front to set expectations.

The drive between Dakhla Oasis and Luxor is pretty long. I recommend starting as early as possible. It is worth paying extra to stay at El Tarfa near El-Qasr. It is a really tastefully designed desert lodge away from the main road. The medieval Islamic trading outpost of El Qasr should not be missed.

Once we got to Bahariya, we went around the villages, took in the sights, hiked up the viewpoints, and meandered through endless miles of date plantations. We ate dates freshly plucked from the trees and took tea in a plantation. It was a very relaxing end to our trip.

On our last day, one of our drivers from the days in the desert came back to our hotel to ensure that our transfer to Cairo went ahead smoothly.

Communication and payment with the owner, Khalid, was very clear, easy, and fuss-free. We paid in USD and in cash once we got to Bahariya.

All in all, the folks at Western Desert Tour were an absolute delight. We all had the time of our lives and we will recommend Western Desert Tours to anyone in a heartbeat.

My husband and I booked a three-day private tour package, and from the very first moment it was clear that this would be an unforgettable experience.
Day 1 – Saqqara, Dahshur & Memphis
Our guide, Dr. Azmy Salama, and our driver, Ahmed (Ghazal), picked us up directly in front of our hotel, and our adventure began. Azmy guided us through the Saqqara necropolis with incredible knowledge and attention to detail, and he took us to the fascinating Serapeum. We then continued to Dahshur, where we explored the Red Pyramid and the Bent Pyramid together, followed by a visit to Memphis.
Already on the first day, we felt completely safe and well taken care of, which was extremely important to us as we do not know the local culture or language. Azmy helped us not only as a guide but also with practical matters that would have taken us much longer on our own, such as buying a SIM card and exchanging money. From day one, we had full trust in both Azmy and Ahmed.
Day 2 – Giza Pyramids & GEM
On the second day, we visited the Giza Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM). This day was especially memorable because it was my birthday. During a coffee break at a local café, Azmy and Ahmed surprised me with a birthday cake and singing — a truly beautiful and thoughtful gesture that made my birthday very special.
Azmy showed us everything in great detail, shared insights and stories we would never have known otherwise, and his guidance through the GEM was excellent and engaging.
Day 3 – Old Cairo, Coptic Cairo & Islamic Cairo
On the third day, we explored Old Cairo, Coptic Cairo, and Islamic Cairo with Azmy. It was another wonderful day filled with history, culture, and meaningful explanations that brought the city to life.
Overall, Dr. Azmy Salama is an outstanding guide — knowledgeable, patient, attentive, and genuinely caring. Together with Ahmed, we always felt safe, relaxed, and welcomed. Thanks to them, we truly fell in love with Cairo. We are leaving Egypt feeling that we have gained not just an amazing experience, but also two friends.
We are already certain that we will return to explore other incredible places such as Luxor, the Valley of the Kings, Abu Simbel, and more — and we would not do it with anyone else.
Highly recommended!

Both evenings, fennec foxes came to visit them (we were really looking forward to meeting them), drank water and ate the leftovers of the chicken. In the morning, around 7 o'clock, you can admire the sunrise in the desert. By this time, a thermos of boiling water is already on the table, you can sip tea and watch a new day begin. What else can I say? The desert is indescribably beautiful, complete silence, you are alone with nature, just you and the desert. We were lucky – there was no wind, it was very quiet and peaceful. It was cool at night (in a sleeping bag + a camel blanket is fine), but in the morning the sand warms up very quickly and it gets warm. The kids went sandboarding down the dunes. Overall, I have only the warmest memories of the trip. I'm already preparing a case study from this journey for my ecotourism lectures at Moscow State University. Thank you for your hospitality and kindness, Loli and Mohammed. We wish you many wonderful guests and hope to see you again!

The Soviet-Egyptian Friendship Monument at the High Dam in Aswan is a must-see attraction for anyone visiting the area. This imposing monument, located on a hill overlooking the dam, was built in the 1970s to commemorate the close relationship between Egypt and the Soviet Union at the time.

The monument itself is an impressive feat of engineering and design, featuring a towering obelisk and a massive statue of two figures holding hands in a symbol of friendship. The surrounding area is also beautifully landscaped, with manicured gardens and walkways that provide stunning views of the Nile River and the surrounding desert landscape.

What I found particularly interesting about the monument was its historical significance. At the time of its construction, it was seen as a symbol of the close political and economic ties between Egypt and the Soviet Union, and a testament to the power of international cooperation. Today, it stands as a reminder of that era and a testament to the enduring friendship between the two countries.
1 hr+

The flavors were rich, authentic, and beautifully balanced, especially the Murgh Tikka Masala and Lasooni Naan, which stood out as favorites. The bhajias were crispy and flavorful, and the Murgh Tikka was perfectly grilled and well-marinated.

A couple of areas for improvement: the Mulligatawny Soup could have been seasoned a bit more to bring out its full depth of flavor. Also, the rice in both the Chicken Biryani and Jeera Chawal was slightly undercooked, which affected the texture of otherwise well-spiced dishes.

Overall, we had a great experience, and would definitely return for another delicious meal. Namaste offers a lovely taste of India in the heart of Cairo – highly recommended for Indian food lovers!

DRIFTING THROUGH TIME - A JANUARYI VOYAGE ON THE NILE

Cruising the Nile from Aswan to Luxor is less a journey and more a graceful immersion into history, geography, and rhythm of the ancient civilisation of Egypt. Our three-day cruise in January—arguably the most pleasant season—combined comfortable weather with luminous skies and calm waters, making the experience both relaxed, enriched and reflective.

Beginning at Aswan and ending at Luxor, the voyage unfolded at an unhurried pace. One of the early highlights was the stop at Edfu, where the proximity of the temple to the river reinforces how deeply the Nile shaped ancient Egyptian life. Equally memorable was crossing the Esna Locks, which in fact is a barrage. What might seem a routine engineering operation turned into a fascinating lesson in river management, navigation, and coordination. Watching multiple vessels queue, negotiate water levels, and pass through in sequence was both entertaining and educational.

Traveling as a large group added a lively social dimension. Conversations flowed easily on deck as the scenery slipped by—lush green banks, date palms, villages, and the occasional felucca. A striking observation was how most cruise ships operate on a synchronized schedule. Many vessels start sailing around the same time, which means actual sailing hours are relatively short compared to the time spent anchored. Yet, this never felt like a drawback. On the contrary, the long anchored periods allowed for excursions, rest, and quiet contemplation of the river.

Life onboard followed a gentle routine: mornings opening to misty vistas, afternoons spent watching the Nile glide past, and evenings marked by soft lights reflecting on water. January’s mild temperatures made deck time especially enjoyable, without the fatigue that harsher months might bring.

Overall, the Nile cruise offered a rare blend of leisure and learning. It was serene without being idle, structured yet unhurried—an experience that lingers long after the river bends fade from view.

What We Loved

1. An Exceptional Guide – Mr. Muhammad Ali (5⭐)

The highlight of our entire Aswan to Luxor tour was undoubtedly our private guide, Mr. Muhammad Ali. From day one, everything was handled with absolute professionalism. The tour was extremely well-organized, perfectly timed, and completely hassle-free. He was always punctual and ensured that every pickup, visit, and transition was smooth and stress-free for us throughout the four days.

What truly sets Mr. Muhammad Ali apart is his deep knowledge of Egyptian history and culture. He didn’t just explain monuments, he narrated Egypt’s journey from over 4,000 years ago to the present day, helping us truly understand and connect with the country. He is equally well-informed about modern-day Egypt, which made conversations with him engaging and insightful beyond just historical facts.

Because of his storytelling and explanations, we felt a genuine connection with Egyptian culture. He truly made our trip memorable and meaningful.
If you are booking through Nile Cruisers, we highly, highly recommend requesting Mr. Muhammad Ali specifically. He is a freelance guide, and you can also spot him in the photos uploaded with our review. Hats off to him, he was one of the best parts of our journey.

2. The Nile Palace Cruise Experience

We stayed on the Nile Palace cruise, and overall, it was a very pleasant experience. The cruise is well-maintained, reasonably renovated, and offers clean, comfortable rooms. The service onboard was good, and the staff was attentive.

The food quality and taste were good, though we felt that the menu selection could be a bit more varied. That said, it did not take away from the overall comfort and enjoyment of the cruise.

Areas for Improvement (Booking & Coordination Process)

The only area where we felt there is room for improvement is the booking coordination and information flow. Some details could have been communicated more smoothly, and we found ourselves needing to follow up to get complete clarity. Reducing the need for follow-ups and providing clearer information upfront would make the experience even better.

Would do it again!

We toured with Egypt Tours Portal from the Delta to Abu Simbel. We're both over 75, one with mobility issues.  Mrs Walaa set an itinerary based on what we thought we wanted, achieving a four-part trip: Cairo (Pyramids), Delta and Alexandria; the "standard" Nile Cruise Luxor-Aswan; a  Lake Nasser Cruise Abu Simbel to Aswan; and back to  (Museums). Originally 13 days, we used an extra day before our flight left to see both the old and GEM museums. We booked privately: there was often just the two of us, occasionally an extra, and on the Nile cruise another couple for part of it.

Most driving was by ETPs minibuses (comfortable, and let you to see over the top  of the traffic); and car to get two of us from Aswan to Abu Simbel for the Lake Nasser cruise. The drivers were all excellent. Special thanks to the clever Mr Wal who got us into places not normally accessed on account of disabilities.

We expected mid-range accommodation, but got top level rooms, andsuites in hotel Concorde El Salam, New Cairo, and the Lake Nasser cruise ship Omar El Khayam.

A multi-part trip, we had a series of amazing guides. Their training and experience showed through all the time: the superbly knowledgeable Ahmad Abo El Magd for initial Cairo and Alexandria, Walid Ahmed guiding us through the standard Nile Luxor-Aswan cruising, Amr Aswany for the museum and other runs in Cairo on return, all from ETP.  Also Bahaa, associated with the Lake Nasser cruise line, guided us and another couple for most of the Abu Simbel to Aswan leg. All showed an uncanny ability to arrange the time and order of viewing to dodge crowds, all treated us to unexpected or unusual things, and all were very protective and caring of us.  Especially for the mobility- and health-limited Deborah, including physical assistance as needed.

Seeing many reviews complaining of guides leading to 'tourist traps"--please, TRUST your Guides! Okay, the emporia they might lead you to might have some spinoff for them--it's how things work!--but they will NOT take you to fleecing shops! Especially for handicrafts, bear in mind the time to make e.g. a rug...then think in terms of salaries, and suddenly the atmospheric price is not all that high for top-end stuff. Also, in many cases the places your guides might take you are co-operatives, and sometimes sheltered workshop outlets. So you're helping as well as paying! and what you get is real and not rubbish! And your Guides WILL protect you from buying overpriced tat made in China in the Bazaar.

Also, the optional excursions guides will offer may or may not appeal, take them as you wish but consider: at Aswan, a bit of extra money got us a private boat to get to Philae and the Botanic Gardens, no need to jostle with 30 other people in general cargo, as it were.

DISABILITY: Deborah has mobility problems which meant slow movement using a rollator, or a pair of sticks with frequent resting. The rollator works fine, with little help, for Cairo and most of Alexandria, but the cruise components have too many stairs and not yet enough ramps. Wheelchairs would have real trouble outside Cairo at present.  Outstanding consideration was given by hotel, ship staff, and outside officials in the Police and Security for the care extended to an elderly lady with mobility problems. No exceptions to this on the whole journey.

This trip was long and multi-part, so inevitably there would be occasional glitches. ETP and our guides were on to it as fast as they could, sorting out the glitch very quickly.

Anyone contemplating this wonderful tour, or one like it, do as we did and start at Alexandria, so the Lake Nasser cruise comes towards the end.  The Luxor-Aswan section is so full on, especially if you take the balloons (you should!) and other optional extras, that you're exhausted by the time you reach Abu Simbel. The more leisurely Lake Nasser run gives the chance to recover.

While many hostels in Egypt offer services to tourist attractions, prices fluctuate significantly. Originally, I only planned to hire a car, but the agency still provided a detailed itinerary.

After comparing prices, I found "Discover Egypt" to be transparent and well-planned. Other agencies seemed to offer lower prices, but they often had hidden fees such as tolls, tips, and extra charges.

The trip went smoothly, and here are some highlights of the agency:

#Itinerary Planning: Efficient communication, completely customized itinerary, and they provided very helpful suggestions. They could help you relax in the hot afternoon, carefully select temples if you felt there were too many, and even arrange visits to shopping malls.

#Airport Pickup Service: Uber isn't allowed in the airport, and hotels overcharge foreigners. The company arranged airport pickup, so you didn't even need to find a driver upon arrival. At the airport, you didn't have to worry about "eager" Egyptians asking for tips for handling your luggage; the pickup staff would find you as soon as you got off the escalator – very thoughtful service. #Local Guide: We originally only hired a car, but we discovered the amazing role of the accompanying assistant. In Egypt, where bargaining is everything, they even managed to ensure you didn't get the foreigner price for water, helping to handle all the details and saving us the hassle of haggling.

#Driver: Three different drivers from the north, central, and south were all punctual, polite, and drove steadily.

#Hot Air Balloon: The hot air balloon ride was rumored to have a murky pricing system, and after the ride, we understood. Other companies' balloons had huge baskets of people, making a bumpy landing. The company arranged a maximum of 8 people, but our family ended up having the whole balloon to ourselves, landing smoothly and gracefully. The local guide even accompanied us from the hotel to the bus and boat, making everything super convenient.

#Meals: Yes, foreigners get tourist prices. We went in with a "let's give it a try" attitude, but the meals were not only convenient but also featured Egyptian specialties and were plentiful.

#Team Communication: Even without Saladin as our guide, we were always there like a magic lamp, able to find someone whenever needed. The assigned bilingual (Chinese and English) guides were very responsible.

Choosing Discover Egypt for this trip was absolutely the right decision! We were two girls traveling together, and from selecting the destination to departure, we only had a month, leaving no time for extensive research. Contacting Discover

For my first trip to Egypt, I opted for a semi-independent tour. Thankfully, after comparing prices from several companies, I finally chose Discover Egypt. The communication process was smooth and quick. Before departure, I had many questions about the itinerary, and everyone patiently answered them, even offering suggestions on the most efficient routes.

Upon arrival, I needed to confirm pick-up times and locations with each tour group beforehand. There were always people handling any issues in the group chat. The guides and drivers were especially punctual, some even arriving early to wait for us at the hotel. Airport pickups were also incredibly smooth. Upon arrival in Cairo and Aswan, as soon as we got off the plane, we saw drivers holding signs with their names waiting at the baggage claim or the terminal exit, saving us a lot of haggling over prices and dealing with locals. The vehicles were all clean and high-end; sometimes they used a nine-seater van for two people, providing ample space for luggage. For tours where we didn't have luggage and needed to move around, they used regular sedans. I felt like a king, enjoying a very comfortable trip.

Especially our Chinese-speaking guide, Jiang Kai, was incredibly meticulous and clear in his explanations. We were often still listening to his stories at the attractions even after other tour groups had left. He was also very patient with our photography, giving us ample time to visit the temples and take pictures. He's also a fantastic photographer; every friend who saw the photos asked if we had brought our own photographer to Egypt. We're so grateful to Discover Egypt for their arrangements. Although we initially thought the price was a bit high, after careful consideration, we realized it was well worth it. In short, I've already recommended Discover Egypt to many friends during my stay in Egypt. I'll write a review later to share my experience, and I hope everyone has a wonderful time in Egypt.

There are no words to describe how helpful and friendly the staff are. They will go out of their way to help you with any problem. Every problem we had, they fix/or tried to fix it quickly. We mentioned how we wanted to try Egyptian desserts and they literally gave us a dessert plate. It was incredibly kind and almost made us cry. lol

The location does suck, however, they’ve fixed that, too. They offer a free, 24-hour driver/shuttle to the sister hotel in the city. They just want an hour in advance or you can WhatsApp them. Was perfect for us and we still did all the things we wanted to do - even at 4 in the morning. They even talked to the tour guide for us in Arabic and made sure everything would go smoothly.

The restaurant was pretty good. Prices are decent for a hotel. The food took a while to come out, but that could be because we got there a little late (around 8:30). TRY THE CHICKEN CREAM SOUP!! So good, I even asked if I could have a bigger bowl - and they did give it to me. They even gave us a dessert that we asked for (uum ali), and that was amazingly good, too.

Room felt pretty nice; clean and maintained. The only thing we didn’t like about it was that the shower glass wasn’t sealed properly and water leaked the whole time we showered. The shower head wasn’t on right because the water kinda sprayed everywhere out of the holes and unevenly. That could just be our room, though.

The WiFi wasn’t good. I was consistently kicked off the WiFi and automatically went to phone data. That’s something that needs to be remedied.

The only other thing would be that the staff needs better English proficiency; they didn’t understand things that we asked about. The staff needs to speak a bit louder, too. Sometimes they spoke too soft and we had to ask multiple times what they said. These things are easily fixed, though. They were still very friendly and kind.

It’s clear that the staff at this location strive for excellence and to make their guests feel comfortable. At first, we thought we made a mistake on going there (as we thought we were at the other location), but after the experience this hotel and the staff gave us - we can say with confidence we made the right choice. If I come back to Aswan, I will choose this hotel again.

I went there in the evening to buy bread to eat on the Abu Simbel tour because of the good reviews on Google, but it was a total rip-off.

This bakery, named "قصر المخبوزات" (literally "Baking Castle"), is located in Aswan, Egypt, and is a traditional bakery and pastry shop brimming with local warmth.

We happened to be passing by, thinking we'd grab some food for the road, and unexpectedly encountered an owner who could communicate in English. He not only patiently inquired about our preferences but also introduced us to the various breads in the shop, even insisting on selling them to us at local prices—some breads were only five Egyptian pounds each, completely unlike the "special prices" often seen in tourist areas.

The bread had a simple, substantial texture with a rich wheat aroma. Although not overly decorated, every bite exuded traditional flavor. However, what truly surprised us were the shop's biscuits and pastries! When we were about to leave Aswan, we went back to find the owner, and this time he not only treated us to tea and biscuit samples but also gave us a large box of pastries. These biscuits were crisp on the outside and soft on the inside, with a subtle hint of spice and honey sweetness. Personally, I thought the biscuits were even better than the bread, and could even be considered a must-buy. Although the staff at the shop don't speak much English, everyone wears a warm smile and conveys kindness through their eyes and body language. Even without a language barrier, you can feel the warmth and hospitality.

If you're planning to buy groceries in Aswan, whether for travel supplies or souvenirs, "قصر المخبوزات" is definitely worth a try. I especially recommend their biscuit series; you might find it even more amazing than their bread, just like I did!

The Temple of Edfu is one of Egypt’s most impressive and best-preserved ancient monuments, making it a must-visit for travelers seeking authentic history and mythology.
Located on the west bank of the Nile between Luxor and Aswan, the Temple of Edfu was built during the Ptolemaic Dynasty between 237 BCE and 57 BCE, taking nearly 180 years to complete. It is dedicated to Horus, the falcon-headed god, who symbolized divine kingship and protection. According to legend, Edfu was the site of the great battle between Horus and Seth, representing the eternal struggle between order and chaos—a story vividly carved into the temple’s walls.
What makes Edfu remarkable is its state of preservation. Unlike many other temples that suffered from erosion or destruction, Edfu remained buried under layers of sand and debris for centuries, which protected its reliefs and architecture. When uncovered in the 19th century, its towering pylons, colossal gateways, and intricate hieroglyphic inscriptions revealed a stunning example of Egyptian religious architecture. Visitors are greeted by two massive pylons adorned with scenes of pharaohs conquering enemies and worshipping gods, flanked by granite statues of Horus. Inside, the temple’s hypostyle halls, sanctuaries, and courtyards reflect the grandeur and precision of ancient Egyptian design.
Edfu offers a rare glimpse into the spiritual life of ancient Egypt. Its inscriptions provide detailed accounts of rituals, myths, and temple practices, making it not only a place of worship but also a historical archive. Walking through its sandstone corridors feels like stepping into a living chronicle of mythology, artistry, and devotion.

SAILING THROUGH TIME - THREE MEMORABLE NIGHTS ON ZEINA NILE CRUISE

As part of a large group touring Egypt in January 2026, we experienced a delightful three-night journey on the Zeina Nile Cruise from Aswan to Luxor. Boarding typically takes place in Aswan sometime around noon on the first day, where the ship remains anchored for the night, allowing passengers to settle in and explore the surroundings at leisure.

Our cruise began sailing on the second day evening around 5 pm. After nearly five hours of smooth travel along the Nile, we reached Edfu at about 11 pm and anchored there overnight. The following morning, we visited the magnificent Edfu Temple before returning to the ship. By late morning, the cruise resumed its journey, crossing the Esna locks around early afternoon and reaching Luxor by about 5 pm. The ship remained anchored in Luxor thereafter, giving passengers ample time to visit the city’s remarkable temples and monuments before disembarking the next day.

The Zeina is thoughtfully laid out. The restaurant occupies the lowest deck, with reception on the ground deck. Passenger cabins are spread across the ground, first, and second floors. The individual cabins are well organised and spacious, with an inbuilt toilet. There are small shops and a conference room on the upper accommodation decks. The open top deck is accessible to all and offers splendid panoramic views of the Nile and riverbanks—an ideal place to relax.

The voyage combined comfort, history, and scenic beauty. We enjoyed every moment of this well-organised and memorable Nile experience. Indeed a memorable and unforgettable sailing in the Nile.
